operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are backtick-quoted in DDL; tables use mixed case (Mailshot_Campaigns, Customer_Addresses, Order_Items) — must preserve original spelling and double-quote in generated SQL.
Tiny DB: every table has 15-20 rows, so read_schema's 300k row cap never triggers; original_values are complete.

DATETIME columns store TEXT like '2018-02-15 09:52:17' (space-separated, no T, no fractional seconds); ts_fuzzer dispatch is 'Date|Number(int elements)' — first element parses as int? No, so Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
customer_login is 100% NULL (distinct=0, storage=['null']) — String sampler gets no elements, p:=1, generates fresh strings; original_values all None.
order_delivered_datetime has distinct=1 (single value '2018-03-20 12:00:00') — Date range collapses to <2 distinct, falls back to 1800-01-01..2100-01-01.
item_status_code distinct=1 ('good'), order_shipping_charges / item_order_quantity are VARCHAR storing numeric-looking text ('85.79','6') — String fuzzer, not Number.
Customer_Addresses, Mailshot_Customers, Order_Items have NO primary key (pk=[]) — sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op; drop_unique_duplicates also no-op (no unique cols).
No composite PKs, no self-FKs, no dangling FKs, no non-unique FK parents — all FKs point to single-column INTEGER PKs that exist.
FK child columns (customer_id, premise_id, mailshot_id, order_id, product_id) are INTEGER NOT NULL but declared type dispatches to Number fuzzer; FK fill overrides with parent values.
product_category appears in both Products ('Food','Electronics',...) and Mailshot_Campaigns ('food','clothes') — case differs; literal-pool anchoring by column name will merge them.
customer_password VARCHAR(10) holds 10-char hex strings; String fuzzer length range [10,11] from elements, but fresh draws use CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() of length in [10,11].
No views, triggers, or indexes beyond PKs in DDL; empty-clone creation is straightforward.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on all DATETIME columns with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S; range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 1929..2018 for date_address_from) — fresh dates stay in that window, plausible.

Number fuzzer on all INTEGER PKs and FK columns: range [-10^0,10^0]=[-1,1] for scale=0 (INTEGER has no args -> scale=0), so fresh PKs are tiny ints {-1,0,1} perturbed — likely collides with existing small PKs, driving PK-duplicate drops.

String fuzzer on VARCHAR columns: 5 sampled originals + distinct pool values, p=0.2 fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with contaminate 0.5 — names/emails/phones become gibberish, likely FN on LIKE/equality predicates over customer_name, customer_email, product_name.

Enum-like columns (payment_method 2 vals, premises_type 3, order_status_code 3, address_type_code 2, outcome_code 2) get fresh random strings w.p. 0.2 — breaks equality predicates like payment_method='Credit Card' -> FN.
customer_login all-NULL: String sampler with no elements -> p=1, always fresh strings; any IS NULL predicate on it becomes FN (no NULLs generated).
order_delivered_datetime single distinct value: Date range fallback 1800..2100, fresh dates wildly out of the 2018 cluster — predicates comparing to '2018-03-20' likely FN.

FK consistency: child draws from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement; since parent PKs are tiny ints and heavily deduped, child FK columns get few distinct values — joins still work but cardinalities skew.
No PK on 3 tables -> no dedup, rows can repeat; COUNT(DISTINCT) predicates may over/under-count vs original.
VARCHAR numeric columns (order_shipping_charges, item_order_quantity) get String fuzzer -> non-numeric text; CAST/arithmetic predicates FN.
Small table sizes (15-20 rows) mean choose_table_sizes produces 30-2300 rows — much larger than original, so COUNT(*) predicates and 'no rows' predicates flip.
Literal pool from train SQL anchors product_category across Products/Mailshot_Campaigns (case mismatch) — pool values may leak 'Food' into mailshot rows, plausible but not original.
Known TS misses: FN from implausible fresh strings on enum/name columns; FP from missing ties (no PK on 3 tables) and from tiny-int PK collisions causing spurious duplicate drops.
